sn47.20:0.3: The Most Beautiful Girl of the Land
sn47.20:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living among the Sumbhas, where there was a town of the Sumbhas named Sedaka.
sn47.20:1.3: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn47.20:2.1: “Bhikkhus, suppose that on hearing, ‘The most beautiful girl of the land! The most beautiful girl of the land!’ a great crowd of people would assemble.
sn47.20:2.2: Now that most beautiful girl of the land would dance exquisitely and sing exquisitely.
sn47.20:2.3: On hearing, ‘The most beautiful girl of the land is dancing! The most beautiful girl of the land is singing!’ an even larger crowd of people would assemble.
sn47.20:2.4: Then a man would come along, wishing to live, not wishing to die, wishing for happiness, averse to suffering.
sn47.20:2.6: ‘Good man, you must carry around this bowl of oil filled to the brim between the crowd and the most beautiful girl of the land.
sn47.20:2.7: A man with a drawn sword will be following right behind you,
sn47.20:2.8: and wherever you spill even a little of it, right there he will fell your head.’
sn47.20:2.10: would that man stop attending to that bowl of oil and out of negligence turn his attention outwards?”
sn47.20:3.1: “I have made up this simile, bhikkhus, in order to convey a meaning.
sn47.20:3.3: ‘The bowl of oil filled to the brim’: this is a designation for mindfulness directed to the body.
sn47.20:3.4: Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus:
sn47.20:3.5: ‘We will develop and cultivate mindfulness directed to the body, make it our vehicle, make it our basis, stabilize it, exercise ourselves in it, and fully perfect it.’
sn47.20:3.6: Thus, bhikkhus, should you train yourselves.”
